aesthetic: Humus — a Swiss-organic visual system where Weingart's typographic confrontation grows from warm earth, treating each slide as a soil cross-section: compressed strata of scale, weight, and silence
chromaticArc: Slides 1–10 breathe on pure Warm Parchment; slides 11–22 introduce Dried Reed and Pale Sage grounds as warmth deepens; slides 23–30 inject Amber Resin and Terracotta accents as tension mounts; slides 31–32 and 40–41 strike with Deep Forest Floor dark grounds as two section-divider confrontations; the final three slides return to Warm Parchment, now weighted with accumulated earth tones in their accents.
gridStrategy: Every slide rotates its dominant axis: a full-bleed vertical title is followed by a hard horizontal split, then a right-anchored fragment with breathing left void, then a bottom-heavy inversion — each new slide's primary zone origin point must differ from the prior slide's by at least 20 columns or 12 rows, ensuring no two consecutive compositions share a spatial signature.

fontStrategy.secondarySlides: Georgia replaces Futura on any slide carrying reflective or testimonial body text (approx. slides 8, 15, 22, 28, 35, 42), signalling a shift from declaration to contemplation; Courier New appears on data-dense or process slides where monospace rhythm reinforces enumeration

accentStrategy: Amber Resin and Terracotta thick bars (span 4–6, full row height) anchor the left or right edge on 55% of slides as a structural spine; Moss Canopy colour blocks (type block, span 8–14) appear mid-composition on section-opening slides to signal growth; single dot elements at col:58 or row:39 act as terminal punctuation on minimalist slides, preserving visual tension without added complexity.
